analysis.title: GS Global 2027 Outlook
key_insights: GS Global Equity Strategy (Peter Oppenheimer) sees a positive backdrop for 2027 with equities moving higher, but with high volatility. The range of potential outcomes has widened.

The 2026 theme of a broadening equity bull market, with more participation across regions, sectors and themes, played out despite rising oil prices and bond yields. Strong corporate earnings growth in all regions was the main driver.
Profit growth and AI capex growth look poised to slow in most regions in 2027. GS says part of this is already priced in, as equity valuations have come down substantially, particularly in Tech.
Moderating inflation, lower bond yields and lower oil prices give a path for the bull market to continue even as growth and earnings slow.
Outcomes depend heavily on AI capex progress, given stock concentration in the US and Asia.
The 2027 theme is 'Finding Value in Growth'. As earnings slow and margins moderate, GS expects investors to pay more for growth companies, particularly as valuations become more attractive.

Some AI companies have already de-rated sharply on anxiety about the pace of AI capex and the possibility of slower returns. GS sees attractive entry points in large-capex Hyperscalers, which have strong balance sheets and diversified income streams.
GS also sees upside in more cyclical growth areas such as memory and chips.
Regional weightings: overweight US and Japan, neutral Asia and EM, underweight Europe. GS says these reflect risk-adjusted returns.
Three investment themes for 2027: Growth, selective Defensives, and beneficiaries of lower oil prices and bond yields.

Value has sharply outperformed Growth across all regions, but Value is no longer as cheap and Growth no longer as expensive on 12m forward P/E premium. Cyclicals have de-rated sharply relative to Defensives.
Global Tech valuations have fallen sharply versus history and other sectors, and the valuation premium of the largest US companies has narrowed.

Charts cited: MSCI AC World P/E and PEG ratios are near their 35-year historical averages, and earnings revisions have been unusually positive. GS top-down estimates show earnings growth more than halving across major markets in 2027, and the Hyperscaler capex contribution to S&P 500 EPS growth is expected to fade.

sector_views.rationale: Valuations have de-rated sharply on AI capex anxiety, leaving attractive entry points in large-capex Hyperscalers with strong balance sheets and diversified income streams.
GS sees upside in more cyclical growth areas such as memory and chips.
Selective Defensives are one of three 2027 themes. Cyclicals have de-rated sharply relative to Defensives.

earnings_insights: GS top-down estimates show 2027 EPS growth more than halving versus 2026 across major markets. The report gives no specific EPS figures in its text.
Consensus MSCI AC World EPS revisions have been unusually positive (consensus estimates in USD). The contribution of Hyperscaler capex to S&P 500 EPS growth is expected to fade in 2027.

macro_indicators.reading: Long-term yields remain elevated, with GS forecasting some relief in 2027. No figure is given in the text.
macro_indicators.interpretation: Lower bond yields and lower oil prices are expected to support equities and are one of the three themes.

macro_indicators.reading: Prices rose in 2026. GS expects them to come down in 2027, with no figure in the text.
macro_indicators.interpretation: Lower oil prices benefit the third theme, beneficiaries of lower oil prices and bond yields.

macro_indicators.reading: GS expects moderating inflation in 2027, with no figure in the text.
macro_indicators.interpretation: Moderating inflation is part of the path for the equity bull market to continue.

risk_factors: A slowdown in AI capex progress, given stock concentration in the US and Asia.
Slower profit growth and moderating margins in 2027.
Wider range of potential outcomes and high volatility.
vol_and_positioning: GS expects equities to move higher in 2027 but with high volatility, and says the range of potential outcomes has widened.
Equity concentration in the US and Asia makes returns particularly dependent on AI capex progress.

tension_points.bull_case: Moderating inflation, lower bond yields and lower oil prices give a path for the bull market to continue despite slower growth. Valuations in Tech and Growth have de-rated, leaving attractive entry points.
tension_points.bear_case: Profit and AI capex growth are poised to slow in most regions, and earnings growth is expected to more than halve. The range of outcomes has widened and depends heavily on AI capex progress.

theme_stances.key_argument: AI companies have de-rated sharply on peak-capex anxiety, leaving attractive entry points in large-capex Hyperscalers with strong balance sheets.
theme_stances.evidence: attractive entry points in large capex Hyperscalers

theme_stances.key_argument: Profit and AI capex growth look poised to slow in most regions in 2027, though some of this is already reflected in valuations.
theme_stances.evidence: profit and AI capex growth looking poised to slow in most regions
